faq: Will you watch my store around the clock?
Not in this order. We set up automatic monitoring that watches around the clock and alerts you. Human response from us is part of our priority support service, quoted separately.
Does monitoring cost extra every month?
Many tools have a free tier that suits one store. If you need a paid plan, you see the price first, and it is billed to you by the tool maker.
What causes my store to go down?
Common causes are host problems, app conflicts, expired domains or certificates and traffic spikes. The response plan covers how to tell which is happening.
Can you monitor a Shopify store?
Yes. Shopify runs its own servers, but your theme, apps, domain and checkout can still fail. We monitor what a shopper sees, which is what counts.

desc:
Store uptime monitoring and alerts tell you when your store goes down or checkout stops loading, before a customer does. Ecom Swift LLC sets up the monitors in your own account and writes a short plan for what happens next.

## What is store uptime monitoring?

Uptime monitoring is a service that visits your store at regular intervals and checks that it responds. If a page fails to load, the service sends an alert by email or phone message. You choose which pages to watch, how often to check and who receives the alert. The tool runs outside your store, so it can still tell you when the store itself cannot.

## Why downtime goes unnoticed

Owners seldom look at their own store at three in the morning. A site can be down overnight, over a weekend or during a campaign, and the first sign is a slump in orders or a message from a customer.

Outages have many causes. A host can have a fault. A domain or security certificate can expire. A bad update, a heavy traffic spike or a failing plugin can bring pages down. A checkout page can fail while the home page loads perfectly, which is why watching only one page is not enough.

## How monitoring protects revenue and reputation

Time is the cost. Every minute a store is unreachable is a minute in which paying ads send visitors to an error. Early alerts shorten that time, because someone starts work while the problem is small.

Monitoring also supports calm decisions. An alert tells you which page failed and when, so you can contact the right party quickly. Over time, the history shows patterns, such as repeated slowdowns at the same hour, which helps you choose a better host or plan. We cannot prevent every outage, since many belong to the host or platform, but we can make sure you hear about each one fast.

## What a good monitoring setup includes

- A monitor on the home page, checked at a regular short interval.
- Monitors on key pages, such as a product page, a collection and the cart.
- A check of the checkout page, since it often fails first.
- Alerts by email and by phone message to the right people.
- A test alert that proves the message arrives.
- Expiry alerts for the SSL certificate and the domain name.
- A status page, public or private, in the larger package.
- A written response plan for your team.
- Slack or Teams alerts where you use them.
- A review of recent downtime history, if the host provides it.

## What we do

We choose a monitoring tool that fits your budget and create the account in your name, so you stay in control. We set up the monitors, pick the check interval and enter the alert contacts. Then we send a test alert, so you know the system works before you need it.

Next we write the response plan. It names who gets told, what we check first and when to contact your host or platform, with a list of the details they will ask for. In Premium, we also create a status page and run a practice incident, so the team has seen the plan work. The monitoring tool runs under your own account, so you can pause or cancel at any time. Round-the-clock human watching is not part of this service. The tool watches, and the plan says who acts.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Send alerts to at least two people.
- Monitor the checkout page as well as the home page.
- Set renewal reminders for your domain and certificate.
- Keep your host's support details in the response plan.
- Test the alert after every change to contacts.

**Avoid:**
- Routing alerts to an inbox that nobody reads.
- Watching only the home page.
- Setting the check interval so long that outages slip through.
- Silencing alerts because of one false alarm.
- Relying on customers to tell you the store is down.

## Who this is for

This suits an owner who runs ads and cannot afford silent downtime. It suits a store that has already had an outage and wants earlier warning. It also suits a seller who travels or works a second job and cannot watch the store all day.

## What we need from you

The addresses of the pages to watch, the names and contact details of the people who should receive alerts, and access as a collaborator or admin user. We do not ask for passwords. Please tell us which host and platform you use, so the plan names the right contact.
